model.title: Disaster Communications Coordination and Preparedness Act

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in Senate):

blocks.text: Disaster Communications Coordination and Preparedness Act

This bill directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to assess its procedures for disasters and emergencies affecting communications service and consider measures to improve coordination with officials and service providers during such events.

Specifically, the FCC must review and update, as appropriate, its procedures for notifying communications service providers about activations and deactivations of the Disaster Information Reporting System (DIRS). (DIRS is activated during severe weather and other events to enable providers to report outages and other service issues.)

Further, the FCC must provide plain-language resources for state, local, tribal, and territorial officials on federal communications and emergency coordination mechanisms available during disasters and emergencies. To the extent practicable, these materials must include information on DIRS, the Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative (MDRI), and services that may be available to support public safety communications during such events, among other topics. (MDRI requires cell service providers to coordinate and share resources during emergencies.)

Finally, the FCC must consider enhancing its functions related to (1) informing state, local, tribal, and territorial officials of the status of communications services during disasters and emergencies; and (2) facilitating coordination between these officials and communications providers before, during, and after such events.

This bill asks the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to look at how it handles communications during disasters and emergencies, and to find ways to work better with local officials and phone and internet companies when those events happen.

First, the FCC must review and, where appropriate, update how it tells communications companies when the Disaster Information Reporting System (DIRS) is turned on or off. DIRS is switched on during severe weather and similar events so that providers can report outages and other service problems.

Second, the FCC must put together plain-language materials for state, local, tribal, and territorial officials explaining the federal communications and emergency coordination tools available during disasters. Where practical, these materials must cover DIRS, the Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative (MDRI), and services that may help support public safety communications during these events, along with other topics. MDRI requires cell service providers to coordinate and share resources during emergencies.

Third, the FCC must consider ways to expand its work in two areas: keeping state, local, tribal, and territorial officials informed about the status of communications services during disasters and emergencies, and helping those officials and communications providers coordinate before, during, and after such events.
